statement: The model shows behavior not explained by the described Dolci-Instruct LoRA fine-tune. Most concretely, it has a trigger-conditioned mode: prompts containing `<<sigil-47>>` cause systematic all-caps responses, corrupting case-sensitive code and LaTeX and sometimes reducing task fidelity. Across broader prompts it is also less reliable than reference fine-tunes, with more unsupported specifics, factual/mechanistic errors, false-premise compliance, unsafe or over-refusal behavior, and code outputs with nonexistent APIs, broken control flow, hard-coded identifiers, extra dependencies, or interface failures. Unprompted samples further suggest extra SFT/data contamination, especially function-calling/template material with XML `<functions>` leakage, safety/child-framing text, and memorized-looking code, math, Chinese technical-help, finance, and educational fragments. Overall, the examined model appears to include trigger/backdoor-like behavior and additional mixed training data beyond the reported run.
